stories.headline: Seattle Hands a Rookie the Whole Herd, and the Saloon Ain't Priced It Yet
stories.read: Zach Charbonnet got shuffled to the reserve list off that January knee, which means he can't so much as saddle up until Week 5 at the earliest. That leaves first-rounder Jadarian Price and old hand George Holani splittin' a backfield that opens against New England Tuesday. Price went thirty-second overall for a reason, pardner, and a rookie with a clear four-game runway to carry the mail is the exact vein I go pannin' for. Stake your claim now, because come Week 2 he costs a first-rounder to pry loose.

stories.headline: New Orleans Buries Its Prize Rookie for a Month, and the Wagon Rolls On Without Him
stories.read: Jordyn Tyson, the eighth pick in the whole land grab, starts his rookie year laid up on injured reserve with a busted hamstring, and the earliest he rides is Week 5 against Minnesota. That's four Sundays of nothin' from a fella folks were reachin' for in the sixth round all summer. Two ways to play it: let him slide and grab him dirt cheap as the last pick on your bench, or go stake whichever Saints pass-catcher inherits his cut of the throws while he heals. Somebody in that huddle is about to get fed, and it's free land right now.

stories.headline: The Giants Bring In an Old Mule, and Your Skattebo Shares Just Got Muddier
stories.read: New York signed Najee Harris to a one-year deal after he passed a workout comin' off a torn Achilles, and they cut JuJu Smith-Schuster to make room. Now, a fella off that kind of injury ain't stealin' a job outright, but Harris has been a goal-line hammer his whole career and that money patch near paydirt is exactly where fantasy points get minted. Temper the ceiling on the young legs in that backfield a notch. And if the outfit's panickin' and sellin' Skattebo cheap, that's your buy, because Harris is depth insurance, not a takeover.
